records.rule: Put set -euo pipefail in executed tools, not in files you intend to source; gate side effects on whether you were executed.
records.source: queuebash.sh (no top set) vs bin/queue-* (set -euo pipefail)

records.rule: To survive a failing child, scope errexit off for it and read its code into rc at once; decode the code into meaning.
Quote every expansion; build commands-to-run as arrays and run "${cmd[@]}" so spaces/newlines stay within one argument.
Expand globs via compgen and filter, and scope IFS to the single delimiter for a structured read; re-read persisted arrays via source + declare -p.
Write a candidate in the destination dir, verify your own output, then publishing with one atomic mv; clean up on every failure.
Validate an all-digits integer before arithmetic; re-normalize; reject a non-positive bound rather than disabling the protection.
Parse exact: both value forms, check arity, reject unknown flags with a usage exit code, and stop at the first positional.
Serialize JSON with a real parser (python heredoc) or bounded backslash-first escaping; keep JSON on stdout and version the schema.
Quote the heredoc delimiter (<<'EOF') whenever the body must be literal; keep an unquoted heredoc only where expansion is wanted.
records.source: providers.d/ask/*.sh static JSON; embedded tool heredocs

records.rule: Treat any provider/remote/renderer output as data, never execute it: no eval, no source, no piped sh, no backtick-into-command.
Treat green test/helper output as evidence for review, never self-authored acceptance or authority.
Deny on ambiguity, malformed input or absence; fail closed and never treat 'no answer' as an allow.
Read/write only paths you verified (object or parent), keep untrusted work in a private workspace, and reject path/type crossings into bare shared scratch.
Verify integrity against a trusted expectation and re-zero the exact variables a record will set before sourcing it.
An external helper cannot exit its parent; propagate with `helper ... || exit $?` or branch on its code yourself.
Keep a one-off mode switch scoped to the single invocation and clear/restore it before later commands.
Try GNU then BSD forms with a safe fallback, and keep scripts LF only (CRLF breaks shebang parsing).
Prefix a domain and an underscore for private helpers, keep a stable public facade, and always declare locals.
